name: ASML Holding N.V.
businessSummary: Sole supplier of EUV lithography systems and a leading supplier of DUV systems to leading-edge semiconductor manufacturers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, etc.).

price.note: EUR, Amsterdam listing. stock-agent showed 1,406.79 for ticker 'ASML' (presumably the Nasdaq USD ADR) -- not reconciled.

sharesOutstanding.note: ~382M implied by market cap/price, not independently confirmed.

netDebt.note: stock-agent ND/EBITDA of -0.67 implies net cash; underlying EUR figure not independently fetched.

enterpriseValue.note: unavailable without a verified net cash figure.

dividendPerShare.note: Q3 2025 interim EUR1.60 confirmed via asml.com press release.

forwardEstimates.source: company guidance: ~15% FY2025 sales growth vs 2024; does not expect 2026 below 2025

recentEvents: Q3 2025: net sales EUR7,516M, net income EUR2,125M, gross margin 51.6%.
Q3 2025 net bookings EUR5,399M, of which EUR3.6B EUV.
Q4 2025 guidance: net sales EUR9,200-9,800M, gross margin 51-53%.
EUR12B 2022-2025 buyback program under-run (only EUR5.9B executed as of Sep 2025); new program to be announced Jan 2026.
valueTrapFlags: Buyback materially behind its own pace/size -- capital-allocation signal to watch.
FY2023 FCF dipped sharply despite revenue growth that year -- working-capital timing issue.
Heavy dependence on a small number of leading-edge customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel).
growthQualityNotes: Revenue growth real: EUR18.6B (FY2021) to EUR32.7B (FY2025), including a near-flat FY2023-24 downcycle then FY2025 reacceleration.
Operating margin range-bound (31-35%) rather than steadily expanding -- a stable-margin, not margin-expansion, story.
FCF volatile due to lumpy working capital tied to large system shipments, but TTM/FY2025 level (~EUR10-11B) suggests durable positive FCF.
dataGaps: Shares outstanding, net debt in EUR, EV, EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA (stock-agent figure discarded), ROIC, ROE, interest coverage, historical multiple range unavailable.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS (EUR), reflecting ASML's range-bound (not expanding) margin profile and lumpy FCF

bear.note: Semiconductor-equipment downcycle repeats (as in FY2023-24), EUV capex delayed by customers.

base.note: AI-driven leading-edge capex continues at a steady pace, similar to the FY2025 reacceleration.

bull.note: AI chip demand drives an extended leading-edge capex upcycle, High-NA EUV adoption accelerates.

valuation.whyItFits: Sole supplier of EUV lithography with effectively no credible competitor, real recent revenue reacceleration (FY2025 +15.6%) after the FY2023-24 downcycle, strong net-cash balance sheet -- the cleanest 'structural moat' growth case on the shortlist, even though margins aren't expanding, just stable.
valuation.growthDrivers: AI/leading-edge semiconductor capex, High-NA EUV system adoption, structural industry reliance on ASML's monopoly position.
valuation.saturation: The FY2023-24 near-flat period shows this is a cyclical-within-structural-growth business -- capex cycles will keep causing lumpiness.
valuation.principalRisk: Heavy dependence on a small number of leading-edge customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel); a slowdown in their capex plans would hit ASML directly, and geopolitical export restrictions remain a standing risk.
